newsitem.title: USA: Columbia/HCA says got three federal subpoenas.
newsitem.headline: Columbia/HCA says got three federal subpoenas.

text.p: Columbia/HCA Healthcare Corp was served on July 16 with three extensive subpoenas and other demands for information by federal authorities investigating the company, it reported Thursday in a filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission.

The SEC 8-K filing confirmed earlier reports that company facilities were searched by federal agents on July 16 in six states: Florida, North Carolina, Oklahoma, Tennessee, Texas and Utah. The filing said the searches occured at 18 Columbia/HCA affiliated hospitals and 15 other Columbia/HCA affiliated locations.
"It appears that the focus of the government's investigation is on outpatient laboratory billing and home health," the filing said, reiterating earlier company statements.
"The company also received three extensive subpoenas from the Department of Health & Human Services' Office of Inspector General," the filing said.
Two of subpoenas focused on the home health investigation and one on the lab billing investigation, the filing said.

Various "authorized investigate demands" were also made by the U.S. Department of Justice in the lab billing probe, the filing said. The company has hired counsel to represent it in both the home health and lab billing investigations.

"Management believes that it is too early to anticipate whether such actions/investigations will have material adverse effect on the company's financial position or results of operations," it said. Shares in the for-profit hospital company -- the largest in the United States -- closed Thursday off 3/16 at 36-3/16 on the New York Stock Exchange. The company was not immediately able to provide more details.
